title: Investigating Effective Ways to Use Artificial Intelligence in Teacher Education
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd European Conference on e-Learning, ECEL 2023
extended_summary:
This paper examines how ChatGPT and related AI tools can be used effectively in teacher education, with a particular focus on lesson planning and classroom activity design. The authors frame the study around a broader concern: how to prepare pre-service teachers to use emerging AI technologies in ways that support equitable education, especially in South African communities that experience resource constraints and digital inequality.

The intervention/approach studied was an AI-supported lesson planning activity in an ICT in Education course. Pre-service teachers generated lesson plans with ChatGPT, then reflected on the outputs through questionnaires and class discussions. The participants were 2nd- and 3rd-year intermediate phase pre-service teachers from a South African teacher preparation program serving marginalised communities.

Findings suggest that ChatGPT can provide useful starting points for lesson plans, content, and assessments, but teachers still need to contextualise and adapt the generated materials to their specific classroom settings. The study also highlights practical implementation features such as using smartphones and mobile apps to access AI tools, and it argues that infrastructure access, connectivity, and needs assessment are important for successful adoption. Overall, the paper concludes that AI can support lesson planning and teacher preparation, but its use must be paired with teacher judgement, local contextualisation, and attention to equity and ethics.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI system for generating and revising text, answering questions, and supporting interactive writing and feedback tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by preservice teachers to generate lesson plans, teaching/learning content, and assessments, and to support lesson-plan development in teacher preparation activities.

findings.finding_summary: In a qualitative study of 2nd- and 3rd-year preservice teachers, participants reported that ChatGPT produced a general lesson plan and relevant content/assessment that provided a useful starting point for contextualising lesson plans to their own classes. Students noted that when they supplied grade level and location, ChatGPT generated more context-specific examples, which they then adapted further for teaching practice.
findings.measure: Preservice teachers' perceptions of ChatGPT-generated lesson plans and content in survey responses and class discussions

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods study using questionnaires and class discussions, so it does not provide experimental causal evidence. The paper reports participant perceptions rather than controlled outcome comparisons.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests useful practical support for lesson planning, but it does not report measurable effect sizes or direct student outcome gains. Impact is therefore plausible but unclear from the evidence provided.
